title: Secondary Academic Logbook PDF Integration & Serial Device Filtering Decision
paragraphs: In today's session, we formally integrated the second official academic project logbook document (logbook2.pdf) into our capstone project repository. This document records our technical progress, software architecture updates, control dashboard testing, and upcoming hardware assembly tasks required for departmental review.

Additionally, we identified and resolved a critical macOS serial port communication issue where virtual Bluetooth audio devices (such as paired Bluetooth speakers and headphones) were appearing as openable serial ports on the Web Dashboard. We implemented strict backend keyword filtering to block virtual system ports and ensure the dashboard auto-detects and connects exclusively to genuine physical USB Arduino Uno hardware.

title: Official Capstone Academic Logbook Integration & Departmental Review Document
paragraphs: In today's session, we formally integrated the official Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering Project Logbook (Log Book-1.docx) into our capstone project repository. This document covers the initial academic project review period from July 20 to July 31, 2026, establishing the formal objectives, guide feedback channels, individual team contribution breakdowns, resource lists, and percentage completion tracking required for university milestone reviews.

The integrated logbook documents our software architecture foundation, hardware workspace preparation, Web Dashboard Phase A construction, and 2-way cloud database synchronization. With official academic reporting artifacts synced directly alongside our web control software, all team members can access and download the official capstone logbook file directly from the project journal interface.

title: Media Payload Overhead, Cloud DB Limits & Text Logger Pivot Decision
paragraphs: During this session, we encountered significant technical friction and engineering overhead attempting to support heavy video clips and multi-device Base64 PDF attachment uploads. Initial integration attempts with third-party file uploaders resulted in unexpected browser ad redirects, broken mobile download links, and device availability failures. Furthermore, attempting to sync 1.5MB+ Base64 PDF DataURLs across cloud database APIs (jsonblob.com) triggered strict HTTP 413 Payload Too Large rejections, HTTP 429 Rate Limiting, and mobile Safari background fetch terminations that blocked form submission and caused cross-device sync inconsistencies between iPhone PWAs and laptop dashboards.

Recognizing that heavy binary media attachments introduced unnecessary complexity, cross-origin security risks, and severe cloud database performance bottlenecks, we made a definitive architectural pivot. We completely stripped all video and file upload inputs from the mobile PWA app and Web Dashboard, streamlining the system into a 100% clean, ultra-fast, zero-friction text logging engine. Essential project documents (such as the college synopsis PDF) will remain managed directly via code integration, while all future session notes will be logged as lightweight, instantly synchronized text entries. This decision restored 0.1-second cloud database sync speeds and eliminated all cross-device storage friction.

title: Interactive Journal App Upgrades, Cloud Sync & Session Finalization Decision
paragraphs: In today's session, we completed the interactive Web Journal PWA and local control dashboard integration. We implemented a real-time header search bar for filtering log entries, instant log entry deletion with cloud database sync, and serverless API integration deployed on Vercel (https://vision-autonomous-robotic-arm.vercel.app). We established a persistent 2-way cloud database sync (jsonblob.com API) so all text journal logs sync seamlessly in real-time across iPhone PWA devices, Laptop Safari, and the local Web Dashboard (http://localhost:8050).

To eliminate cross-device media storage overhead, we streamlined the mobile journal into a clean, ultra-fast text logging engine, reserving document attachments (such as the college synopsis PDF) to be managed directly via session code integration. With full web documentation, cloud sync, and dashboard software locked in place, we finalized Session 5 to transition our full technical focus to physical 6-DOF robotic arm hardware assembly.

title: Physical Workspace Geometry & Dual-Frame Calibration Decision
paragraphs: In this session, we finalized the physical workspace geometry and perception pipeline in preparation for hardware assembly. We established persistent REST endpoints for saving physical link measurements and servo zero offsets to a persistent configuration file. The Web Dashboard layout was further refined by placing the 3D Digital Twin tab in the final sidebar position, updating its sync status to "Standing By (Awaiting URDF)", and anonymizing all interface text to ensure a clean, presentation-ready capstone interface. Additionally, we added individual "Test Solo" diagnostic buttons to each servo card for single-joint assembly testing and configured Uvicorn live auto-reload on port 8050.

A major focus of this session was establishing the planned workspace coordinate blueprint for the 50cm x 50cm wooden platform (note that currently only the bare wooden board exists; no ArUco markers have been printed or attached yet). We finalized a dual-frame transformation architecture: ArUco Marker ID 2 will be placed at the corner of the platform near the overhead camera pole, establishing a rock-solid World Frame Origin (0,0). This design ensures that every point on the platform map has strictly positive coordinates (X, Y from 0 to 50cm) and prevents the robot arm from casting shadows over the calibration marker. The exact physical mounting position of the Robot Base on the board will be measured and registered in software once physical assembly and mounting is complete, allowing Python to convert vision coordinates into robot-centric vectors before executing Inverse Kinematics calculations. We also generated vector SVG ArUco markers, created a printable 4cm x 4cm HTML sheet, and compiled a step-by-step physical assembly guide.

title: Web Dashboard Construction & Pre-Assembly Preparation Decision
paragraphs: This session focused on transforming the control software into a full-featured, web-based robotic dashboard to support the entire project lifecycle, starting with physical hardware assembly. Built with FastAPI, WebSockets, and a custom warm linen design system, the dashboard provides live joint sliders, zero-jerk S-curve automated routines, and automated serial port detection via the Arduino CLI tool. We integrated live PS5 DualSense controller teleoperation directly into the web browser via the Gamepad API and added a dedicated Kinematic Calibration panel to tune physical link lengths and servo zero offsets in real-time.

To support team integration, a dedicated top-level 3D Digital Twin tab was created to host the 3D URDF simulation model. We implemented individual "Test Solo" diagnostic buttons for single-joint physical assembly testing and generated vector SVG ArUco markers alongside a printable HTML sheet. Finally, we confirmed the Stage 1 environment design—keeping the destination box fixed while randomly placing the sponge block—to establish a clean, high-accuracy baseline before introducing multi-object complexity in Stage 2.

title: Capstone Documentation & Setup Visualizations Decision
paragraphs: During this session, attention shifted toward project documentation and presentation materials. We drafted comprehensive prompts for AI generation tools to produce a professional presentation slide deck for the college synopsis defense. Visual design specifications were defined for creating high-impact 3D render prompts depicting the complete dual-camera robotic workbench setup. The synopsis PDF was finalized and submitted to the university department, establishing a clear project schedule across the six-month development timeline.

title: Architecture Definition & Firmware Foundation Decision
paragraphs: The project began with a thorough architectural review of the 6-DOF robotic arm capstone project. We established the core hybrid perception and control strategy, deciding to isolate vision feature extraction using OpenCV before passing compact coordinate data into a neural network trained via Behavior Cloning. To ensure human teleoperation produces clean, natural motion, we agreed to implement Cartesian Inverse Kinematics driven by a PS5 DualSense controller rather than relying on direct joint manipulation. On the hardware front, we selected lightweight sponge cubes with cardboard-backed ArUco markers to prevent servo stall and eliminate surface warping under variable room lighting.

For safety and embedded control, we designed a dual-layer safety mechanism featuring a physical emergency stop switch alongside a 500ms serial watchdog on the Arduino Uno. Firmware scripts were developed for initial servo zeroing and production binary packet driver execution. Additionally, we resolved a key mechanical assembly strategy: rather than mounting joints strictly straight up at 90 degrees, we decided to mount hardware at physical midpoints to maximize workspace reach, allowing software joint offsets to handle the mathematical mapping seamlessly.
